description: Our group is made up of students who are about to take their Baccalaureate exams at the end of this year. We come from Morocco, we are all high school students, and we share a common love for astronomy, space, and science. We have just started our journey and are still new, but we are eager to learn more and explore further.
summary: INFECTIUM is an educational survival game where children aged 7–12 restore an abandoned lunar outpost. The journey starts in a proportionally scaled Solar System, then follows an Artemis-style trajectory to the Moon. Players balance oxygen, water, energy and food, and must also protect the crew from radiation. That radiation is driven by real NASA DONKI space-weather data (coronal mass ejections, solar flares, geomagnetic storms, solar energetic particles), refreshed live during play. Space-quiz questions earn the “knowledge” points needed to unlock new buildings and upgrades. The project makes space-weather risk, one of the real obstacles to living on the Moon, tangible and fun, and aims to make children love astronomy. If NASA data is unavailable, the game switches to a clearly labelled SIMULATED mode.
details:
What it does. INFECTIUM is a browser-based mission trainer. Players travel from the Solar System to the Moon, then renovate an abandoned base (hub, nursery, water purifier, solar array, forge) while managing O₂, H₂O, energy, food and radiation in real time. Correct quiz answers raise a “cultural level” that works as currency to unlock new tiers.

Use of NASA data. The NASA DONKI API (CME, FLR, GST, SEP) is fetched during play and aggregated into a radiation level. That level continuously increases consumption of oxygen, water, energy and food, and is reduced by the Hub’s shield level. APOD and NeoWs complement the briefing panel. The NASA API key stays server-side in a Netlify Function.

Impact. Children learn that space weather is a real constraint of lunar exploration, in a game built around curiosity.

Tools. React, Vite, TypeScript, Three.js, Netlify (hosting + Functions).

Creativity. One continuous scene, from galaxy to Moon surface, with real data driving gameplay and a transparent LIVE/SIMULATED badge.

Design choices. Gameplay parameters (recovery rates, building sizes, incident probabilities) are game design values, not official NASA figures.
